doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Great Lakes band: A, B and C bands and jam sessions
summary: Panken lists notable Navy musicians; Donaldson was in the young C band and sneaked into jam sessions with the older players.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years

blocks.x: Ok. I’d read 1944 somewhere. There were a lot of musicians who were legitimate musicians at Great Lakes.
Some of the names I have are Willie Smith, great alto player.
Talk a bit about how the band were set up, the types of things they played, the functions they played.
What they did, after they broke down the bands, they had about ten bands. Now,

these guys you’re talking about were a little older than me. They played in a band they called the A-band. Then they had another band. The guys were a little older. The B band. I was in the C band, because I was 18, and most of the guys in the band where I was were 18 years old. We were young people. But at the end of all the rehearsals and everything during the day, they’d have jam sessions, so we’d go and sneak on in, and play with the big boys...
It was great. A great set-up.
What sorts of things were they playing then?
Whatever was happening during that day. “Take The A Train,” “Satin Doll,” stuff like that. “Stompin’ at the Savoy.” A lot of stuff.
